topics.name: Platform Overview & Navigation
topics.description: Learn what the ServiceNow AI Platform is, how instances work, and how to move around with Next Experience Unified Navigation: the All, Favorites, History and Workspaces menus, the filter field, and global search.

introduction.overview: Platform Overview and Navigation covers what the ServiceNow AI Platform is, what a ServiceNow instance is (including cloning and Admin Center), and how users find their way around with Next Experience Unified Navigation. That includes the All, Favorites, History and Workspaces menus, the filter field, the scope and update set picker, global search, and user preferences.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 7% of the current CSA exam blueprint (January 2026). It has fewer questions than other domains, but everything else on the exam assumes you can move around the platform quickly and know how instances relate to each other.
introduction.keyConcepts: Know what each Unified Navigation menu does, how the filter field works (for example table.list and table.do), how favorites and history behave, what the application scope and update set picker controls, and how instance cloning overwrites the target instance.
introduction.examTips: Watch for questions that test default behavior, for example which menu the filter field ignores or which preference categories only admins see. Know the difference between the All menu and the Favorites menu, and what a clone does to data on the target instance.

keyConcepts: All, Favorites, History and Workspaces menus

topics.name: Instance Configuration
topics.description: Install applications and plugins, personalize and brand the instance, work with system properties, and understand the common user interfaces: Core UI, Next Experience, workspaces and Service Portal.

introduction.overview: Instance Configuration covers installing applications and plugins (Application Manager, the ServiceNow Store, and plugin activation), personalizing and customizing the instance (system properties, Theme Builder, basic configuration and branding), and the common user interfaces: Core UI, Next Experience, configurable workspaces and Service Portal.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 10% of the current CSA exam blueprint (January 2026). Admins install applications, change system properties and pick the right interface for each audience, so expect practical questions about where and how these things are configured.
introduction.keyConcepts: Know the difference between applications and plugins (including that plugins can't be deactivated), how demo data works, what system properties do, what Theme Builder is for, how application scope works, and which interface fits which audience.
introduction.examTips: Read carefully for which tool is used where. Store applications are installed through Application Manager, some plugins have to be requested, and the scope picker controls where configuration changes are recorded.

keyConcepts: Application Manager and the ServiceNow Store

topics.name: Lists, Forms & Collaboration
topics.description: Configure lists, filters, tags, forms, form templates, task management, assignment rules, Visual Task Boards and notifications. Part of the Configuring Applications for Collaboration domain.

introduction.overview: This topic covers most of the Configuring Applications for Collaboration domain: lists, filters and tags; list and form anatomy; form configuration with Form Builder; form templates and saving options; task management (the Task table, assignment and data lookup rules); Visual Task Boards; and notifications.
introduction.whyItMatters: Configuring Applications for Collaboration is 20% of the current CSA exam blueprint (January 2026). Together with the Reporting & Dashboards topic, it makes up one of the two largest non-security domains.
introduction.keyConcepts: Know how filters, breadcrumbs and the condition builder work, the difference between personalizing and configuring lists and forms, how templates and Insert vs Insert and Stay behave, how Task table inheritance works, the three types of Visual Task Board, and the parts of a notification (when to send, who receives it, what it contains).
introduction.examTips: Many questions hinge on who a change affects: personalization affects only you, and configuration affects everyone. For notifications, remember recipients aren't filtered by ACLs, and don't send notifications on the Task table itself.

topics.name: Visualizations, Dashboards & Analytics
topics.description: Build visualizations and dashboards, understand Platform Analytics and report security. Part of the Configuring Applications for Collaboration domain.

introduction.overview: This topic covers the Visualizations, Dashboards, and Platform Analytics part of the Configuring Applications for Collaboration domain: creating data visualizations, report sources, drilldowns, dashboards in the Platform Analytics experience, Analytics Center, and how Performance Analytics tracks trends over time.
introduction.whyItMatters: Visualizations and dashboards are one of the listed subtopics of the Configuring Applications for Collaboration domain, which is 20% of the current CSA exam blueprint (January 2026).
introduction.keyConcepts: Know that data visualizations replace legacy reporting in the Platform Analytics experience, how report sources work, how report security and sharing work, when drilldown is not supported, and the difference between point-in-time reports and Performance Analytics trends.
introduction.examTips: Expect navigation questions (where to find Data Visualizations and Analytics Center) and 'which tool' questions (a one-time report versus trending with Performance Analytics).

topics.name: Self Service & Automation
topics.description: Knowledge Management, Service Catalog, Workflow Studio and Virtual Agent: articles and workflows, catalog items, record producers, order guides, variables, flows, triggers and topics.

introduction.overview: Self Service & Automation covers Knowledge Management (knowledge bases, article workflows, user criteria, feedback and versioning), Service Catalog (catalog items, record producers, order guides, variables and variable sets, categories, user criteria, Catalog Builder), Workflow Studio (flows, subflows, triggers, actions, flow logic, spokes) and Virtual Agent (topics and natural language topic discovery).
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 20% of the current CSA exam blueprint (January 2026). Self-service and automation are how most organizations get value from the platform, so expect scenario questions about choosing the right tool.
introduction.keyConcepts: Know the difference between a catalog item, a record producer and an order guide; what variable sets are for; how Can Read and Can Contribute user criteria control knowledge access; the Instant Publish and Approval Publish workflows; the parts of a flow (trigger, actions, flow logic); how subflows differ from flows; and that Virtual Agent conversations are built from topics.
introduction.examTips: Scenario wording matters. 'Create an incident from the catalog' points to a record producer, 'order several items at once' points to an order guide, and 'reuse the same questions across items' points to a variable set. Remember that flows only run once they're activated.

keyConcepts: Catalog items, record producers and order guides

topics.name: Data Schema, Importing Data & CMDB
topics.description: Tables, fields, table extension, dictionary overrides and the schema map; importing data with import sets, transform maps and coalesce; CMDB and CSDM basics. Part of the Database Management and Platform Security domain.

introduction.overview: This topic covers the data half of the Database Management and Platform Security domain: the data schema (tables, fields, system fields, table extension, dictionary overrides, relationships, the schema map), importing data (data sources, import set tables, transform maps, coalesce, transform scripts), and CMDB and CSDM basics (CI classes, relationships, IRE, CMDB Health, CSDM domains and service types).
introduction.whyItMatters: Database Management and Platform Security is the largest domain on the current CSA exam blueprint (January 2026), at 30%. The blueprint places Importing Data in this domain.
introduction.keyConcepts: Know base, parent and child classes, the required system fields, when to use a dictionary override, the relationship types (reference, glide list, many-to-many, database view), how coalesce decides between insert and update, and the difference between cmdb_ci and cmdb_rel_ci. Know what CSDM is for.
introduction.examTips: For imports, think through what happens with no coalesce, single-field coalesce and multiple-field coalesce. For schema questions, remember that dictionary changes on a parent table affect every child table unless there's an override.

keyConcepts: Table relationships and the schema map

topics.name: Access Control & Platform Security
topics.description: ACLs, roles and groups, elevated roles, impersonation, Security Center and the Shared Responsibility Model. Part of the Database Management and Platform Security domain.

introduction.overview: This topic covers the security half of the Database Management and Platform Security domain: application and access control (ACLs, decision types, table and field ACLs, roles and groups, elevated privilege roles, role delegation, impersonation), Security Center (hardening compliance score, security scanner, best practices) and the Shared Responsibility Model.
introduction.whyItMatters: Database Management and Platform Security is 30% of the current CSA exam blueprint (January 2026), the largest domain. Access control questions come up often and need precise knowledge.
introduction.keyConcepts: Know that a user must pass every condition in an ACL, that table ACLs are evaluated before field ACLs, that Deny-Unless ACLs are evaluated before Allow-If ACLs, that ACLs are deny by default, that you elevate to security_admin to create ACLs, why roles should be assigned to groups, and what the customer and ServiceNow are each responsible for under the Shared Responsibility Model.
introduction.examTips: Be precise about ACL evaluation order and outcomes. Remember that client scripts and UI policies are not security controls. Security Center questions usually test what the hardening compliance score and the security scanner show.

topics.name: Data Migration & Integration
topics.description: UI policies and data policies, business rules, system update sets, and scripting basics: client scripts, script includes, GlideRecord and background scripts.

introduction.overview: Data Migration and Integration covers UI policies (and when to use a data policy instead), business rules (when they run, execution order and recursion), system update sets (capturing, completing, previewing, committing, merging and backing out changes), and scripting in ServiceNow (client scripts, script includes, GlideRecord, g_scratchpad and background scripts).
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 13% of the current CSA exam blueprint (January 2026). These are the tools admins use to change platform behavior and move configuration safely between instances.
introduction.keyConcepts: Know UI policy options (Reverse if false, On load, Order, Inherit), before, after, async and display business rules, the order in which scripts and engines run, what update sets capture (configuration, not task data), the dev to test to prod path, and the client script types (onLoad, onChange, onSubmit, onCellEdit).
introduction.examTips: Know which tool fits the scenario: a UI policy for form behavior, a data policy for all data sources, a before business rule to change the current record, and an update set to move configuration. Remember that update sets don't track table deletions.
